title: Rights in statute and common law

match.reason: The new point covers how courts protect rights through common law as well as parliament's statutes, but the closest bank point, leg-statutes-that-protect-rights, covers only statutes, so it is narrower and no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Rights in statute and common law
card: Law made by parliament. Parliaments can protect rights by passing acts, such as anti-discrimination acts, that ban unfair treatment in areas like work and education.
Law developed by judges in court cases. Courts can protect rights through their decisions, such as the right to a fair trial.
Parliament can change or override common law by passing a statute. A court cannot override a valid statute by common law.
Both sources can protect rights. A person whose rights are breached may use a statute, or a court may apply a common law principle.
draft.remember: Parliaments protect rights by making statutes. Courts protect them through common law decisions.

a.q: Which example shows a right being protected by statute law?
opts: Parliament passes an act banning disability discrimination
A judge applies a rule from earlier court decisions
A court decides a case on a fair trial principle
A tribunal member gives a personal opinion on fairness
a.why: A statute is made by parliament, and an anti-discrimination act is one. The judge's rule and the fair trial decision come from courts, so they are common law. A personal opinion is not law.

b.q: A court's common law ruling gives a person less protection than they want. Parliament then passes an act giving more protection. What is the effect?
opts: The statute prevails over the common law ruling
The common law ruling prevails over the statute
The two cancel out and neither applies
The court must first approve the statute
b.why: Parliament can change or override common law by passing a statute. The common law ruling does not defeat a valid statute, and courts do not need to approve it first.
b.clue: Which source can change the other?

a.best: Parliament passes an act banning disability discrimination

b.best: The statute prevails over the common law ruling
